components.note: 发 (fā) gives a sound related to fèi, sharing the initial f-, though the rhyme has drifted from ā to èi over time.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
日 here pictures a person's head.
共 pictures two hands; together with the shape below, they depict a violent struggle, giving 暴 its meaning 'violent, sudden.'
雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.
纟 (silk) — 绅 originally named the silk sash worn by officials.
申 (shēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 绅.
中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to chóng, sharing the same rhyme.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
讠 (speech) — 词 names a word, a unit of speech.
司 (sī) gives the sound — an exact match with 词.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
皿 (dish) — 盘 names a flat dish or tray.
般 (bān) gives a sound distantly related to pán, having drifted apart over time.
八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.

components.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
又 (hand, here standing in for 奚, part of the original character) — a simplified stroke that no longer pictures anything on its own.
鸟 (bird) — combined with the simplified left side, 鸡 names a specific 'kind of bird,' the chicken.
虫 (a small creature) — 蛋 names an egg, historically grouped together with small creatures like insects and reptiles.

歹 (death/bad) — 残 relates to damage, destruction, and injury.
戋 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to cán, having drifted apart over time.
刃 (blade) pictures something sharp and painful.
心 (heart) below suggests bearing pain in one's heart, giving 忍 its meaning 'to endure.'

聂 (niè) gives a sound distantly related to shè's reading, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 造's meaning 'to make, build,' an action carried through to completion.
告 (gào) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zào.

讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.

宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.

亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'

良 (liáng) gives a sound close to niáng, sharing the same rhyme.
氵 (water) — the water something sinks into
冗 (excess/heavy) — the excess weight that pulls it down
黑 (black/dark) pictures nightfall.
犬 (dog) pictures a dog keeping silent watch in the dark, giving 默 its meaning 'silent, still.'

羊 (yáng) shares the rhyme family -ang with xiáng, though the initial has drifted from y- to x- over time.
纟 (silk/thread) — 细 relates to something as fine and thin as silk thread

Gives the sound jiān, related to xián but drifted apart over time.
疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating

辶 (to walk) — 迹 names the trace left behind by walking.
亦 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to jī, having drifted apart over time.

礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.

圣 is the simplified form of 聖, which combined an ear (耳, listening) and a mouth (口, speaking) above a standing figure — the image of someone who listens and speaks with special insight, giving 圣 its meaning 'holy, sacred.'
穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.
亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')
敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
